ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin, and the vertex A of the rhombus OABC has coordinates (3, 4). Connect OB and AC to intersect at point H. Draw line $BD \parallel AC$ passing through point B to intersect the x-axis at point D. Find the equation of line BD.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral OABC is a rhombus, \\
it follows that OB$\perp$AC, \\
and since BD$\parallel$AC, \\
it also follows that OB$\perp$BD, that is $\angle$OBD$=90^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle$OBF+$\angle$DBF$=90^\circ$, \\
and since $\angle$DBF+$\angle$BDF$=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle$OBF$=\angle$BDF, \\
furthermore, since $\angle$OFB$=\angle$BFD$=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\triangle$OBF$\sim$$\triangle$BDF, \\
thus, $\frac{OF}{BF}=\frac{BF}{DF}$, \\
leading to $\frac{8}{4}=\frac{4}{DF}$, \\
from which we solve that DF$=2$, \\
therefore, OD$=$OF$+$DF$=8+2=10$, \\
thus, D(10,0). \\
Suppose the equation of the line on which BD lies is $y=k_{1}x+b$, \\
substituting B(8,4), D(10,0) into the equation gives $\begin{cases}8k_{1}+b=4\\ 10k_{1}+b=0\end{cases}$, \\
solving this yields $\begin{cases}k_{1}=-2\\ b=20\end{cases}$. \\
Therefore, the equation of line BD is $\boxed{y=-2x+20}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin, and the vertex A of the rhombus OABC has coordinates (3, 4). Connect OB and AC to intersect at point H. Draw line $BD \parallel AC$ passing through point B to intersect the x-axis at point D. Find the equation of line BD.
raw_record.answer: Solution: Since quadrilateral OABC is a rhombus, it follows that OB$\perp$AC, and since BD$\parallel$AC, it also follows that OB$\perp$BD, that is $\angle$OBD$=90^\circ$, therefore, $\angle$OBF+$\angle$DBF$=90^\circ$, and since $\angle$DBF+$\angle$BDF$=90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle$OBF$=\angle$BDF, furthermore, since $\angle$OFB$=\angle$BFD$=90^\circ$, it follows that $\triangle$OBF$\sim\triangle$BDF, thus, $\frac{OF}{BF}=\frac{BF}{DF}$, leading to $\frac{8}{4}=\frac{4}{DF}$, from which we solve that DF$=2$, therefore, OD$=$OF$+$DF$=8+2=10$, thus, D(10,0). Suppose the equation of the line on which BD lies is $y=k_{1}x+b$, substituting B(8,4), D(10,0) into the equation gives $\begin{cases}8k_{1}+b=4\\ 10k_{1}+b=0\end{cases}$, solving this yields $\begin{cases}k_{1}=-2\\ b=20\end{cases}$. Therefore, the equation of line BD is $\boxed{y=-2x+20}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description first: The figure shows a Cartesian coordinate system with O at the origin. The rhombus is ordered O-A-B-C: A is above and to the right of O, C lies on the positive x-axis, and B is above the x-axis to the right. The diagonals OB and AC are drawn and meet at H. A line through B goes downward to meet the x-axis at D, and it is drawn parallel to AC. There is also an extra curve labeled y = k/x near B, but it is not needed for finding line BD.

Reasoning: From the problem text, A = (3, 4), OABC is a rhombus, and BD is parallel to AC. Since OA is a side of the rhombus, |OA| = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5. From the figure, C lies on the positive x-axis and OC is an adjacent side of the rhombus, so OC = 5 and C = (5, 0). In the parallelogram/rhombus with adjacent vertices A and C from O, the opposite vertex is B = A + C = (3, 4) + (5, 0) = (8, 4). The slope of AC is (0 - 4)/(5 - 3) = -4/2 = -2. Since BD is parallel to AC, line BD has slope -2 and passes through B = (8, 4). Using point-slope form: y - 4 = -2(x - 8), so y = -2x + 20.
